system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: SCATTERING is a novel technique that dynamically varies input prompts when sampling from LLMs, driving more diverse and exploratory outputs.
system_prompt_style.note: Paper only; prompts vary per branch with directions, seed instructions and global SCOUTING insights. The system prompt itself is not described.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: the solver is given a prompt p in natural language, which asks the solver to write code for some object s.
env_context_strategy.note: Function-level code generation from the task prompt only; there is no repository. Paper-only evidence.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; there is no code or config surface where history handling would be declared.

observation_format.evidence_quote: feedback from validation tests → propose new textual directions using LLM
observation_format.note: Test feedback is inferred to be text.

tool_call_format.note: Paper only; the output parsing format is not described. The LLM emits code directly.

tool_count.note: No tool registry is available (paper only).

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Given a parent solution si and its feedback fi, the LLM producesk child solutions
edit_primitive.note: Each child is a complete new solution.

protocol_standardization.note: No code or dependency list is available.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Our method incorporates three optimization inspired techniques to enhance both exploration and exploitation of tree search (MCTS) using LLMs.
loop_primitives.note: MCTS over refinements driven by validation-test feedback, with multiple seed solutions (foresting).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: querying the LLM to generate possible improvement directions [d]n first. The LLM is then instructed to implement a specific direction dj
planning_granularity.note: Directions are per-step text rather than a stored plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: the LLM functions as the optimizer

delegation_mechanism.note: No agent factory is visible (paper only).

short_term_state.evidence_quote: bQ(s, d) is the estimatedq-value which is updated via backpropogation
short_term_state.note: MCTS tree with visit counts and q-values, plus a global insights memory.

long_term_memory.note: The global insight memory is within-task; nothing is said about persistence across runs.

self_verification.note: Validation tests are LLM-generated and executed; the pass fraction is the value.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Methods were given the same search budget (10 solutions)
retry_policy.note: The budget is 40 in the Table 4 setting.

rollback.evidence_quote: We take the max of bQ(si, di+1)(t) and bQ(si+1, di+2)(t+1) to ensure that if the next solution is worse, the current solution can be used instead.
rollback.note: Backtracking happens in the search tree, not via file rollback. Coded none; arguably not_reported.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: We run each method for 10 iterations.
termination_condition.note: The run presumably also stops once all validation tests pass, but this is not stated.

execution_isolation.note: The test execution environment is not described.

eval_hooks.note: The paper evaluates on HumanEval, MBPP and others, but no repo is available to check for built-in hooks.

target_domain.evidence_quote: We frame code generation as a black-box optimization problem within the code space
target_domain.note: The domain is function-level code generation, not repositories; swe is the closest value.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025

first_release_date.note: The v1 date is not in the evidence; only v2 (25 Feb 2025) is shown.

pinned_version.note: Paper version only; there is no repo.
